description: Solo-developer team passionate about aerospace engineering, low-level systems, and data visualization. Developing the Lunar Landing Site Navigator for the NASA Space Apps Challenge an advanced mission planning tool that computes real-time solar ephemeris, axial tilt, and LOLA terrain relief masking to optimize Artemis and CLPS South Pole landings. Focused on technical precision, interactive 3D terrain rendering, and robust mission constraints evaluation.
summary: The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an advanced mission-planning web application designed for Artemis and Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) missions targeting the complex South Pole of the Moon. It addresses the challenge of balancing critical mission constraints by computing real-time analytical ephemeris (leveraging JPL Horizons), modeling axial tilt, lunar libration, and applying local LOLA terrain relief masking to simulate true horizon clearance. The application features a 360-degree interactive topographic horizon profile canvas, a Three.js 3D South Pole terrain visualizer with dynamic solar rays and Earth Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication vectors, and a rapid trade-off comparison matrix. By providing instant evaluation of solar illumination, sunset countdowns, and communication visibility, it serves as an essential decision-support tool to optimize landing site selection and operational safety.
details:
What it does and how it works:

The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web-based mission planning dashboard tailored for lunar South Pole exploration. It allows mission planners to select curated candidate sites (such as Shackleton Rim or Malapert Massif) or input custom latitude and longitude coordinates alongside a target landing epoch date. Using analytical ephemeris models, it calculates real-time solar elevation, Earth Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight angles, and power generation potential. It integrates local Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA topographic relief masking to dynamically plot a 360-degree local horizon profile and render a 3D interactive terrain mesh using Three.js, complete with real-time vector lines for solar rays and DTE communication links. Additionally, it includes a 30-day operational window analysis and a rapid trade-off comparison matrix to evaluate alternative site-date scenarios side-by-side.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The tool directly solves the critical challenge of extreme lighting conditions and communication dropouts at the lunar poles. By instantly identifying regions of permanent shadow, near-eternal light, and Earth visibility constraints, it helps mission architects maximize solar power harvesting and maintain continuous telemetry links, drastically increasing mission safety and success rates for Artemis and CLPS stakeholders.

Tech Stack & Tools Used:

-Languages & Core: JavaScript (ESM), HTML5 Canvas, CSS3.

-Frameworks & Libraries: Vite (development build tool), Three.js (3D South Pole terrain and vector rendering).

-Ephemeris & Topography Data: Analytical models derived from JPL Horizons, NASA Moon Trek, and LRO/LOLA datasets.

-AI Assistance: Utilized Large Language Models (LLMs) to accelerate code structuring and documentation refinement.

Creativity and Considerations:

The project stands out by combining high-precision astrodynamics and topography masking into a lightweight, client-side web application without heavy backend dependencies. Careful consideration was given to UI/UX design, adopting a professional "mission control" aesthetic optimized for clarity, speed, and real-time trade-off analysis.
